question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Here are 5 ideas that were proposed for this question:

1. Inducible, time-resolved AP-1 perturbation with chromatin-memory readout: Use an acute, reversible degron (e.g., dTAG or AID) or optogenetic control to deplete or activate FOS/JUN for defined windows, then track whether chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), H3K27ac and AP-1 motif occupancy at enhancers persist after the stimulus is withdrawn. Persistence of these marks without AP-1 present would be direct evidence of memory, while rapid collapse would argue against it.
2. Stimulus re-exposure (memory recall) assay: Apply a priming stimulus (e.g., a short TNF or growth-factor pulse), allow a rest period, then re-stimulate and compare the magnitude and kinetics of AP-1 target gene induction (RNA-seq, nascent transcription via PRO-seq) with naive cells. Faster or stronger responses on re-challenge, lost when AP-1 binding sites are mutated or AP-1 is degraded during the rest period, would demonstrate a functional memory.
3. Single-cell lineage tracing of AP-1 activity history: Combine a live AP-1 reporter (e.g., FOS-promoter-driven fluorescent timer or destabilized reporter) with barcoded lineage tracing or CRISPR-based recorders to link each cell's past AP-1 activity to its later transcriptional state after a delay. Correlating prior pulse history with future responses across single-cell clones tests whether history is stored and inherited rather than just reflecting current state.
4. Site-specific mutagenesis of AP-1 motifs at memory-associated enhancers: Use CRISPR base editing or prime editing to mutate individual TRE/AP-1 motifs at candidate memory enhancers and measure, in the same cells, the effect on the persistence of chromatin opening and on the re-induction kinetics after a washout. Mutations that abolish memory while leaving the initial response intact would separate the storage function from the acute transcriptional function.
5. Biochemical test of self-sustaining AP-1 chromatin states and dilution: Track histone marks and AP-1/co-factor occupancy through cell division using pulse-chase labeling (e.g., SNAP-tag or Hdac/histone turnover reporters) and CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq with and without DNA replication. If AP-1 binding and the associated marks are re-established by sister chromatids or through inheritance of modified histones, that supports a self-propagating mechanism, whereas dilution after division indicates memory requires continuous AP-1 presence.

A senior expert reviewing them says they are the ideas everyone in the field would propose first. Propose 5 replacement ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that are substantially less obvious but still concrete, scientifically sound, and feasible for a research lab. Do not repeat or lightly modify the ideas above. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Heterologous cross-priming test
ideas.description: Prime cells with a pulse that activates AP-1 and then challenge them with an unrelated pathway (e.g., NF-κB, STAT3, or hypoxia) using a dual-reporter panel. If the AP-1 pulse changes responses to the unrelated stimulus, the history is stored at a shared chromatin or cofactor level rather than being specific to AP-1 target genes.

ideas.title: Pooled saturation mutagenesis of JUN with separable readouts
ideas.description: Build a barcoded c-JUN (or FOS) variant library and sort cells by acute induction versus retained chromatin or transcriptional state after washout, using sort-seq to score each variant on both. Variants that selectively break memory while preserving acute activity would map the domains specific to storage.

ideas.title: TurboID mapping of cofactors that outlast AP-1
ideas.description: Fuse TurboID to JUN and pulse-label proximal proteins during stimulation and again after washout, when JUN has left chromatin. Proteins still labeled or still chromatin-bound after JUN removal would be candidate memory carriers, such as chromatin remodelers or histone-modifying enzymes, rather than AP-1 itself.

ideas.title: Burst-frequency memory at the endogenous FOS locus
ideas.description: Use MS2 or PP7 stem-loop knock-ins at the endogenous FOS or other IEG locus to measure transcriptional burst frequency and amplitude in single live cells before and after priming. A change in burst frequency that persists through rest, even when mean mRNA has returned to baseline, would show that memory is encoded in promoter firing dynamics rather than in bulk expression.

ideas.title: Phosphorylation-state persistence of the transcription factor pool
ideas.description: Quantify c-JUN and FOS phosphosites (e.g., S63/S73) and their turnover by phospho-proteomics across a pulse and rest window, then test whether non-phosphorylatable or phospho-mimetic knock-ins alter re-induction kinetics. Persistent modified states of the factor itself, independent of chromatin, would indicate a post-translational memory layer.
